The function \(f(n)\) interprets the base-10 digits of \(n\) as a number in base \(b\), where \(b\) is one more than the largest digit of \(n\). For \(f(n)=n\) to hold:

- If \(n\) is a 1-digit number, \(n = d\) (\(1 \le d \le 9\)). Then \(b = d+1\) and interpreting the single digit \(d\) in base \(d+1\) gives \(d\), so all 1-digit numbers satisfy \(f(n)=n\). There are \(9\) such numbers.

- If \(n\) is a 2-digit number \(n = 10a+b\) (\(a \ge 1\)), the equation \(a(b+1) + b = 10a + b\) (with \(b = M+1\), \(M = \max(a,b)\)) forces \(M=9\). Thus \(n\) must contain the digit 9. Among 2-digit numbers (10 to 99), those with at least one 9 total \(90 - 8 \times 9 = 18\).

- If \(n\) is a 3-digit number \(n = 100a+10b+c\) (\(a \ge 1\)), the equation \(a(M+1)^2 + b(M+1) + c = 100a + 10b + c\) reduces to \((M-9)[a(M+11)+b]=0\), which forces \(M=9\). Thus \(n\) must contain at least one 9. Among 3-digit numbers (100 to 999), those with no digit 9 are \(8 \times 9 \times 9 = 648\), so those with at least one 9 total \(900 - 648 = 252\).

Adding them gives \(9 + 18 + 252 = 279\).

\boxed{279}
